subject: Transfer routing & TIA scope — NovasysHealth residency checkpoints
messages:
From: Priya Menon <priya.menon@novasyshealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, May 6, 2026 at 09:12 -0700
Subject: Data transfer routing and TIA scoping for NovasysHealth

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal asked me to send a concise list of routing/transfer questions to help scope the TIA + DPA addendum work for our EU footprint. Attached is a very small transfer matrix (initial-transfer-matrix.csv) showing where our users live and which endpoints they hit.

High level asks from our side:
- Does Redwood support a configurable onshore fallback so we can guarantee EU-only processing for traffic originated from the EU?
- If a UK Addendum is needed, what artifacts do you provide for the UK IDTA/UK Addendum signoff?
- For a TIA/DTIA, what sample size of traffic/echos do you typically provide (token sampling, audit logs)?
- Can you provide a list of subprocessors with residency flags (onshore/offshore)?

Can you propose a short plan and an estimated 2-week timeline for the initial gating artifacts? We want to bundle this with our procurement run.

Thanks,
Priya
Priya Menon
Head of Privacy Ops, NovasysHealth
attachments: initial-transfer-matrix.csv (CSV)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@novasyshealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, May 6, 2026 at 13:30 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing and TIA scoping for NovasysHealth

Hi Priya — thanks for the clear list and the matrix. Looping in Laura (legal) and Kimberly (infra) to cover the two rails (legal artifacts + infra evidence).

Quick proposed orchestration (short):
1) Discovery (2 business days): we review the matrix and confirm ingress regions, endpoint patterns, and identify any multi-hop subprocessors.
2) Evidence bundle (5 business days): Redwood provides a TIA scoping outline, a subprocessors list with residency flags, a sampling plan (tokens + request traces), and a stub DPA addendum checklist showing where the UK Addendum would slot in.
3) Technical verification (3 business days): infra provides example logs (redacted) showing request routes, KV cache residency behavior, and audit log retention windows; legal prepares redline notes for the DPA/UK Addendum.

Immediate asks from us to speed this up:
- Confirm the three primary ingress regions (EU country codes) and an example API path used in production.
- Indicate whether you need signed liability redlines up front (helps prioritize legal sequencing).

I've attached a one-page outline for the TIA scoping (TIA-scoping-outline.pdf) — this is intentionally a strawman. If that looks reasonable, we can begin the evidence sprint tomorrow.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Manager, Sales Engineering — Redwood Inference
attachments: TIA-scoping-outline.pdf (PDF)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@novasyshealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, May 7, 2026 at 08:45 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing and TIA scoping for NovasysHealth

Priya / Jordan — legal here. A few clarifications from our side to scope the UK Addendum and any DPA redline work:

- UK Addendum vs SCCs: If NovasysHealth has EU-resident users only, SCCs + UK Addendum may still be required for UK-resident accounts; please confirm whether you expect UK-resident data in scope.
- Evidence we need for signoff: subprocessors CSV (with roles and residency), a copy of retention/audit-log policy, and a confirmation of KMS/HSM custody model for keys (if you require HSM-backed custody we can show our integrations).
- Sampling: legal typically requests a conservative sampling plan for the TIA — we propose 3% of active sessions over a 7-day window (redacted), with token-level aggregates and request trace ids.
- DPA redlines: please flag any non-starters (e.g., unlimited liability, data-exit timing under 30 days).

We can produce a UK Addendum evidence checklist once we have the subprocessors CSV and the KMS statement. Jordan, Kimberly: can infra provide a short statement on audit-log retention and whether logs can be partitioned by tenant/region?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference>
To: Priya Menon <priya.menon@novasyshealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference>
Date: Sat, May 8, 2026 at 10:03 -0700
Subject: Re: Data transfer routing and TIA scoping for NovasysHealth

Hi all — infra notes below, high level and deliverable-oriented.

- Onshore fallback: Redwood supports region-based routing policies. We can pin EU-origin traffic to EU-only model variants and provide a documented fallback policy if EU capacity is exhausted (fallback stream goes to dedicated EU pool first; global fallback is configurable but we can show logs proving EU routing precedence).
- KV cache & prefix caching: residency of caches is configurable; for strict onshore-only requirements we can enable EU-local caches with eviction/replication rules.
- Logs & sampling: we can emit request traces with stable ids and provide token-aggregate telemetry. We typically deliver sanitized request traces (request_id, timestamp, ingress_region, model_id) plus aggregate token counts.
- Subprocessors: attached is an updated transfer matrix with a preliminary subprocessor residency column (transfer-matrix-updated.csv). Note this is a living doc — we'll add a full subprocessor CSV export for legal.
- KMS/HSM: we support customer-managed KMS via our Private offering and integrate with common cloud KMS providers; HSM-backed keys are available on dedicated contracts — will state this in the evidence bundle.

Next steps I can own: produce a 3-page infra evidence pack (logs template, cache residency statement, sampling artifacts) within 3 business days after we confirm the ingress country list.

Kimberly Park
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: transfer-matrix-updated.csv (CSV)
